title: autotune: cost optimization defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults for batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost
- Introduce quantization profile templates and selection heuristics
- Add unit-economics analysis tooling and a CLI report command
description:
Motivation: Reduce unit inference cost by providing safer defaults and automation for batching/caching, quantization profile selection, and unit-economics tooling. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) New 'autotune' defaults for batching and KV caching that prefer lower-latency-safe batching thresholds and enable prefix caching heuristics; 2) A set of quantization profile templates (int8/llm/q4/ggml-style) and lightweight heuristics for choosing a profile based on workload characteristics (seq distribution, model size, accuracy budget); 3) Unit-economics tooling (CLI + backend) to estimate per-request token cost given current cluster config, predicted batching behavior, and quantization choices.

What changed: Implemented runtime defaults and a new Autotune service that calculates per-model recommendations; added quant_profiles/* JSON templates; added redwood/tools/uecon CLI to generate CSV/JSON reports and integrate into the Console; expose an API endpoint /v1/admin/autotune/recommendations. Include migration that writes recommended defaults to model config only after a canary evaluation. Tests and benchmarks included (unit, integration, perf-canary workloads). See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.

Testing: Unit tests for heuristics, e2e tests against perf-canary harness, baseline cost regression checks. Benchmarks show average per-token spend reduced by ~16% on typical chat workloads and latency percentile impact <5% at P95.

Rollout: Feature gated behind 'autotune' flag; staged rollout via canary job and monitored UEcon dashboards. Ops playbook added to docs. Related Linear: ENG-4123 (autotune core), ENG-4187 (uecon tooling).
